ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The diagram shows a right triangle with a marked right angle between a horizontal side and a vertical side. A semicircle labeled X is drawn on the horizontal side, a semicircle labeled Y is drawn on the vertical side, and a larger semicircle labeled Z is drawn on the slanted hypotenuse. Reasoning: Let the horizontal leg, vertical leg, and hypotenuse have lengths a, b, and c. These are the diameters of the semicircles. A semicircle with diameter d has area (1/2)π(d/2)^2 = (π/8)d^2. Therefore X = (π/8)a^2, Y = (π/8)b^2, and Z = (π/8)c^2. Since the triangle is right-angled, a^2 + b^2 = c^2. Multiplying by π/8 gives X + Y = Z.

method.method_draft: Read the diagram as a right triangle whose horizontal leg carries semicircle area X, whose vertical leg carries semicircle area Y, and whose slanted hypotenuse carries semicircle area Z. From the text, use that the three triangle sides are exactly the diameters of the three semicircles. Let the horizontal, vertical, and hypotenuse lengths be a, b, and c. A semicircle with diameter d has area (π/8)d^2, so X=(π/8)a^2, Y=(π/8)b^2, and Z=(π/8)c^2. Since the triangle is right-angled, a^2+b^2=c^2. Multiplying by π/8 gives X+Y=Z.

method.method_draft: Read the picture first: the two smaller labeled semicircles X and Y are drawn on the perpendicular sides of the right triangle, while the larger labeled semicircle Z is drawn on the slanted side opposite the right angle. From the text, treat each triangle side as the diameter of its corresponding semicircle. Instead of computing the semicircle formula, use the generalized Pythagorean theorem: for any three similar figures constructed on the sides of a right triangle, the area of the figure on the hypotenuse equals the sum of the areas of the corresponding figures on the legs. All semicircles are similar figures, so the semicircle on the hypotenuse has area equal to the sum of the semicircle areas on the two legs. Therefore X+Y=Z.
